A1.justification: Both complete 30-page PDFs describe the same SMPE2 study. Pages 2-30, including Appendices A-F, match exactly in extracted text and rendered appearance. Page 1 differs only in affiliation and publication information.

before.justification: v1 reports original MARL experiments on MPE, LBF and RWARE, with benchmark results, ablations and additional analyses in Section 4 and Appendices B and E.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original benchmark experiments, ablations and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The state-modelling framework, encoder-decoder, agent-modelling filters, critic losses and intrinsic exploration procedure remain identical, including Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same MPE Spread and Double Speaker-Listener scenarios, six LBF tasks and three hard RWARE tasks. Appendix coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Figures 2-4 retain MAA2C, COMA, MAPPO and ATM, plus EOI, EMC and MASER for LBF/RWARE. The SIDE, MLIAM and appendix comparisons also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain average episodic reward as the primary metric and budgets of 10M steps for MPE/LBF and 40M for RWARE. Experimental settings and hyperparameters in Appendices E-F are identical.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix E.4 retain the same component and critic ablations, loss-weight sensitivity tests, embedding analyses, intrinsic-reward diagnostics and MAPPO-backbone experiment.

E5.justification: Section 4 reports averages over six random seeds and the same stated 25-75% confidence intervals in both versions. Uncertainty displays are unchanged.

E6.justification: Learning curves, numerical entries and qualitative findings are identical throughout both versions, including the appendix accuracy and runtime results in Tables 1-2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, optimization objectives, Proposition 2.1 and its Appendix D proof are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning state modelling, adversarial exploration and benchmark performance.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and result interpretations are identical. The future questions about scalability and stochastic settings, and the Impact Statement's applicability caveats, also remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix F and Tables 3-7 retain identical implementation details and hyperparameters. Hardware specifications, runtime information and code-access disclosures are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, bibliography and research positioning in the main text and Appendix A are identical.

P1.justification: Page 1 expands ETH Zurich to Department of Mathematics, ETH Zurich, changes the conference ordinal from 41st to 42nd, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded affiliation changes line wrapping in the first-page footnote, and the vertical arXiv stamp changes. All figures, tables and the layout of pages 2-30 remain identical.

improvement.justification: v2 makes only first-page affiliation and publication-information edits with minor associated formatting changes. The scientific content, empirical evidence, proofs and reproducibility information remain identical, so overall paper quality does not meaningfully change.
